citation: Chang SS, Chen YY, Yip PSF, Lee WJ, Hagihara A, Gunnell D. Regional changes in charcoal-burning suicide rates in East/Southeast Asia from 1995 to 2011: a time trend analysis. PLoS Medicine. 2014;11(4):e1001622. doi:10.1371/journal.pmed.1001622.
title: Regional changes in charcoal-burning suicide rates in East/Southeast Asia from 1995 to 2011: a time trend analysis
abstract: Regional observational analysis of the spread and timing of charcoal-burning suicide across East and Southeast Asia.
population: populations of selected East and Southeast Asian countries
intervention_or_exposure: regional adoption and spread of charcoal-burning suicide
comparator: countries and periods with differing charcoal-burning trends
uncertainty: Observational regional trend analysis cannot estimate the effect of a specific retail restriction intervention.
Coding practices for charcoal-burning suicide varied across countries.

evidence_claims.statement: Charcoal-burning suicide rose markedly in several, but not all, East and Southeast Asian settings, with substantial variation in timing and scale across countries.
evidence_claims.population: populations of selected East and Southeast Asian countries
evidence_claims.intervention_or_exposure: regional adoption and spread of charcoal-burning suicide

provenance.locator: PubMed PMID 24691071, Abstract: Results and Conclusions

evidence_claims.statement: Increases in charcoal-burning suicide were associated with increases in overall suicide in some settings but not consistently across all countries and demographic groups.
evidence_claims.population: populations of selected East and Southeast Asian countries
evidence_claims.intervention_or_exposure: regional adoption and spread of charcoal-burning suicide

limitations: Variation in coding practices and data completeness across countries.
applicability: Provides epidemiological context for why means-restriction policies may have different relevance across regions.
safety_boundaries: Do not infer individual suicide risk from regional trends.
